label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To whoever's been putting their rubbish in the bin at No. 14,

I'm not going to dress this up. Someone on this terrace has been filling my bin with their own black bags every week for about a month now, and I've had enough of it.

It's not the odd bit of rubbish thrown in when there's room. It's full bags. Last Tuesday I got home from work at 3 in the morning and couldn't close the lid because there were three bags in it that weren't mine, one of them full of nappies. Lovely thing to find at that hour.

I'm with Greenmount, so I'm charged by weight, 41c a kilo. My bill is usually around €25 for two months. The last one was €63.20. So I'm paying for your rubbish, and I'm not doing that anymore.

In case anyone thinks it's someone passing through, one of the bags had a gas bill envelope in it. The name was torn off but the address was still on it, and it's this terrace. A neighbour also saw a car pull up on Tuesday evening. So it's someone who lives here, knows which night the bins go out, and is counting on me not noticing.

I noticed. The bin has 14 painted on the lid in big white letters, so nobody can say it was a mistake.

If you're stuck because you don't have a bin, can't afford one, or don't know how to sort one out, fair enough, it happens. Knock in and ask me. I'll tell you who to ring. It's one phone call and it's not hard.

I'm not looking for an apology or a confrontation. I just want it to stop. If it keeps happening, I'll be putting a padlock on the bin, which is a pain for me and shouldn't have to come to that.

I work nights, so I'm up and about a lot later than most people on this road. I'm easygoing, but I'm not a pushover, and I'm not going to keep footing the bill for someone else's mess.

Sort out your own bin. Simple as.

No. 14

---

It comes to about 370 words. I left your name off and just signed it "No. 14" since it's going in every letterbox, but you can add your name if you want.
